errors: Expected resistant cells: 10¹⁰ × 1/10⁸ = **about 100**, present *before* the first dose. (This is the expected number of mutation events. Early mutants multiply, so the expected number of resistant cells is larger.)
Expected resistant cells before any drug: 10^10 × 10^-9 = 10. (This counts mutation events, not resistant cells. Early mutants leave many descendants.)

Then every cell would have the same chance to survive. Instead, a rare fraction survives, and those cells were resistant before they met the drug. (A small uniform chance also predicts a rare surviving fraction. Luria-Delbrück's evidence was the variance between cultures, not the rarity of survivors.)

Change the target | The target protein changes shape, so the drug cannot bind | MRSA makes a cell-wall enzyme that penicillin-type drugs do not bind (MRSA acquires an extra enzyme, PBP2a, that beta-lactams bind poorly. No existing target changes shape.)

why_best: A gives the reader every step in a short, error-free chain (pre-existing variation with worked numbers, selection with a regrowth calculation, a quantitative Luria-Delbrück refutation of the adaptation idea, and horizontal transfer across species) and defines each term once, without detours.
